stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Average Tempo in Recordings of Brandt's Violin Sonata (beats per minute)
Movement | Recorded 1930–1959 | Recorded 1990–2019
I (Allegro) | 132 | 144
II (Adagio) | 44 | 60
III (Rondo) | 152 | 156

Musicologist Rafael Okafor timed forty commercial recordings of Ottilie Brandt's 1887 Violin Sonata. Half were made between 1930 and 1959, and half between 1990 and 2019. Later performers, he observes, sped up every movement, but the change was largest in the slow Adagio. Okafor concludes that modern players treat the Adagio as singing rather than mourning: in the recent recordings, the movement averages ______ beats per minute.
explanation: The statement asks about the Adagio in the recent recordings. Find row II (Adagio), go across to the 1990–2019 column, and you get 60 beats per minute.

A.why: You worked out how much the Adagio sped up (60 − 44 = 16). The statement asks for the tempo the recent recordings average, not the size of the change.

B.why: You read the correct row but the wrong column. 44 is the Adagio's tempo in the 1930–1959 recordings, not the recent ones.

D.why: You read the correct column but the neighbouring row. 144 is the Allegro's tempo in the 1990–2019 recordings, not the Adagio's.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: Archaeologist Ines Calloway examined linen fragments from five medieval sites in a single river valley. Brisk Ford, at the river mouth, was a busy seaport where imported cloth was common. Arnhal, Coldwater, Dunmere, and Eskby lay inland. Calloway argues that fine weaving was not limited to the port. As evidence, she notes that among the inland sites, fragments from ______ had the highest average thread density.

figure.caption: Average Thread Density of Linen Fragments by Site
figure.alt: Bar graph of average threads per centimeter in linen fragments from five sites: Arnhal, Brisk Ford, Coldwater, Dunmere and Eskby.

explanation: The phrase "among the inland sites" leaves out Brisk Ford. Of the four inland bars, Dunmere's is tallest at 32 threads per centimeter, so Dunmere completes the statement.

A.why: You took the bar next to the right one. Arnhal's fragments average 28 threads per centimeter, which is below Dunmere's 32, so Arnhal is not the densest inland site.

B.why: You picked the tallest bar on the whole graph and ignored the words "among the inland sites." The passage says Brisk Ford was the seaport, so it is outside the group the statement asks about.

D.why: You reversed the comparison. Eskby has the lowest thread density of any site, not the highest among the inland ones.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Workers Holding Two or More Jobs (% of industry workforce)
Year | Retail | Transportation
2004 | 9 | 6
2008 | 11 | 8
2012 | 12 | 10
2016 | 12 | 13
2020 | 13 | 15

Labor economist Mira Szabo tracked the share of workers holding more than one job in two industries. App-based delivery work spread quickly during the 2010s. Szabo hypothesizes that it drew transportation workers into second jobs at higher rates than before. Consistent with this, she notes that the rate for transportation workers first rose above 10 percent in ______.
explanation: Go down the Transportation column and find the first value greater than 10. The figure for 2012 is exactly 10, which does not exceed 10. The next row, 2016, shows 13. The rate therefore first rose above 10 percent in 2016.

A.why: You read the Retail column. Retail first rose above 10 percent in 2008, but the statement is about transportation workers, whose rate that year was only 8 percent.

B.why: You treated reaching 10 percent as rising above it. In 2012 the transportation rate was exactly 10, so it had not yet gone past 10 percent.

D.why: 2020 is when the transportation rate was highest. The statement asks when it first went above 10 percent, which happened one row earlier, in 2016.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: A comet's tail forms when sunlight and the solar wind push gas and dust away from its nucleus. Both forces are strongest at perihelion, the comet's closest approach to the Sun. However, heat takes time to reach a comet's buried ice. Astronomer Leandro Vey therefore predicted that the tail of comet C/2031 K4 would reach its greatest length only after perihelion. His measurements bear this out: the tail was longest ______ days after perihelion.

figure.caption: Tail Length of Comet C/2031 K4
figure.alt: Line graph of the comet's tail length in millions of kilometers, measured every 5 days from perihelion to 25 days after perihelion.

explanation: Find the highest point on the line, at 16 million kilometers. Then read straight down to the horizontal axis. That point sits at 10 days after perihelion.

A.why: Day 0 is perihelion itself. On that day the tail was at its shortest, 6 million kilometers, and the passage says the measurements showed the peak came after perihelion.

C.why: You read the point next to the peak. At 15 days the tail had already shrunk to 14 million kilometers.

D.why: 16 is the peak's value on the vertical axis, in millions of kilometers. The statement asks how many days after perihelion the peak occurred, which you read from the horizontal axis.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Average Streamflow on the Teller River (cubic meters per second)
Month | Above reservoir | Below dam
February | 40 | 48
April | 120 | 80
June | 90 | 70
August | 25 | 50
October | 35 | 45

Hydrologist Amara Djalo compared streamflow at two gauges on the Teller River over the same year. One gauge was above Fenwick Reservoir and the other directly below its dam. The dam stores spring meltwater and releases it gradually. As a result, Djalo argues, flow below the dam does not drop as sharply in late summer as flow above the reservoir does. Even so, the gauge below the dam recorded its lowest monthly flow in ______.
explanation: The statement is about the gauge below the dam, so use only the "Below dam" column. Its smallest value is 45 cubic meters per second, in the October row.

A.why: You chose a nearby value that looked smallest. February's 48 is slightly higher than October's 45, so February is not the lowest month below the dam.

B.why: You reversed the comparison. April has the highest flow below the dam, 80 cubic meters per second, not the lowest.

C.why: You read the "Above reservoir" column, where August's 25 is the lowest value. Below the dam, August's flow was 50, one of the higher readings.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Archaeologist Nadia Farouk dug three trenches into Tell Saruq, a settlement mound, and sent charcoal from each of three stacked soil layers for radiocarbon dating. Deeper layers were laid down earlier. Farouk argues that people settled the mound's northern edge, where Trench B was cut, before they settled anywhere else on the site. In support, she notes that charcoal from the lowest layer of Trench B was dated to ______ years before present.

Charcoal Sample Ages at Tell Saruq (years before present)
Layer | Trench A | Trench B | Trench C
Upper | 2,140 | 2,310 | 2,060
Middle | 2,880 | 3,020 | 2,750
Lower | 3,460 | 3,710 | 3,390
explanation: The statement asks for the lowest layer of Trench B. Find the Lower row and the Trench B column. They meet at 3,710, which is also the oldest date in the table, so it supports Farouk's claim.

A.why: You used the right column but read the Upper row. The passage says the sample came from the lowest layer, not the top one.

B.why: You read the Trench B column one row too high. 3,020 is the Middle layer, not the Lower one.

C.why: You used the right row but slipped one column to the left. 3,460 is Trench A, not Trench B.

Mean Antibody Concentration (units/mL)
Week after dose | Standard formulation | With adjuvant
2 | 48 | 95
6 | 120 | 210
12 | 85 | 160

B.why: You read the right row in the wrong column. 120 is the standard formulation group, which received no adjuvant.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: On Gull Key, foxes that raid nests had kept a colony of least terns small for years. After the 2018 breeding season, wildlife managers built a fence across the island's narrow neck to keep foxes out. With fewer nests lost to predators, more adult terns would survive to return and breed. Ecologist Mara Lindqvist observes that in the first breeding season after the fence was built, the colony held ______ nesting pairs.

figure.caption: Least Tern Nesting Pairs on Gull Key, 2016–2022
figure.alt: Line graph of the number of least tern nesting pairs on Gull Key each year from 2016 to 2022.

explanation: The fence went up after the 2018 season, so the first season after it was built is 2019. The point for 2019 sits at 60 nesting pairs.

A.why: 35 is the value for 2018. The fence was built after that season, so 2018 is the last year before the fence, not the first year after it.

B.why: 55 is the value for 2017, two years before the first season with the fence. You read the wrong point on the line.

D.why: 70 is the 2020 value, the highest point on the graph. You went for the most striking number instead of the year the statement names.

stimulus:
In 2024, planners in the city of Brantford added protected bike lanes, separated from traffic by curbs, to four busy corridors. They counted weekday bicycle trips on each corridor the year before construction and again the year after. Planner Joan Okafor points to Harbor Road, which had the most daily trips of any corridor once the lanes opened, where average weekday trips reached ______.

Average Weekday Bicycle Trips by Corridor
Corridor | Before lanes (2023) | After lanes (2025)
Elm Avenue | 410 | 980
Harbor Road | 620 | 1,140
Mill Street | 350 | 520
Pine Boulevard | 780 | 1,010

B.why: You read the right column but the row above Harbor Road. 980 belongs to Elm Avenue.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
In 2023, the city of Larkfield painted protected bicycle lanes on three commercial streets. Planners counted cyclists on each street on weekdays, once in the spring before the lanes opened and again a year later. City engineer Dalia Osei said the results were uneven: Elm Street changed most, partly because it links two large residential districts. In her report, Osei concluded that on Elm Street, the average number of weekday cyclists rose by ______.

Average Weekday Cyclists
Street | Before lanes (2023) | After lanes (2024)
Elm Street | 340 | 910
Harbor Avenue | 280 | 520
Mill Road | 410 | 700
explanation: The claim is about Elm Street only, and it asks how much the count rose, so you need the gap between Elm Street's two values. In the Elm Street row, the count went from 340 before the lanes to 910 after. 910 − 340 = 570.

A.why: You worked out the gap for Mill Road (700 − 410) when the claim is about Elm Street. You read the right column but the wrong row.

C.why: You took Elm Street's 'after' value (910) but subtracted Harbor Avenue's 'before' value (280). Both numbers have to come from the same row.

D.why: 910 is Elm Street's count after the lanes opened. The claim asks how much the count rose, so you need the difference, not one of the two values.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: Recordings of a well-known piano sonata have slowed over the past century. Musicologist Henrik Vasquez timed the opening movement in dozens of commercial recordings and averaged the tempos by decade. He links the trend to the spread of historically informed performance, which encouraged pianists to let individual phrases breathe. According to Vasquez, the average tempo of recordings from the 1930s was faster than the average tempo of recordings from the 1990s by ______ beats per minute.

figure.caption: Average Tempo of Opening Movement in Recordings, by Decade
figure.alt: Bar graph of average tempo in beats per minute for recordings from the 1930s, 1960s, 1990s and 2020s.

explanation: The claim compares two decades, the 1930s and the 1990s, and asks how much faster the earlier one was. The 1930s bar is at 132 beats per minute and the 1990s bar is at 108. 132 − 108 = 24.

A.why: You compared the 1930s with the bar right next to it, the 1960s (132 − 120). The claim names the 1990s, two bars further along.

C.why: You compared the 1930s with the 2020s (132 − 102). You used the last bar instead of the 1990s bar the claim names.

D.why: 108 is the 1990s tempo itself. The claim asks how much faster the 1930s recordings were, so you need the gap between the two bars, not the height of one.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Earthworms loosen soil and pull crop residue underground, so farmers watch their numbers closely. Agronomist Priya Natarajan divided a field into plots that were treated the same except for one thing: whether a cover crop grew there over the winter, and which one. She counted earthworms in each plot in spring and again in fall. Natarajan reported that in fall, plots with a clover cover crop held ______ as many earthworms as plots with no cover crop.

Earthworms per Square Meter
Plot treatment | Spring | Fall
No cover crop | 18 | 24
Clover cover crop | 54 | 96
Rye cover crop | 36 | 60
explanation: The claim names the fall column and compares the clover row with the no-cover-crop row. In fall, clover plots had 96 earthworms per square meter and plots with no cover crop had 24. 96 ÷ 24 = 4, so the answer is four times as many.

A.why: You compared clover with rye (96 ÷ 60). The claim's baseline is plots with no cover crop, not the other cover crop.

B.why: You read the rye row (60 ÷ 24) instead of the clover row it sits next to. That is rye's ratio, not clover's.

C.why: You used the spring column (54 ÷ 18). The rows are right, but the claim is about fall.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Purple sea urchins graze on kelp, and where they crowd together, kelp forests can thin to bare rock. In 2023, marine ecologist Tala Moreno surveyed four reef sites along a rocky coastline. At each site she counted urchins in plots at two depths. Moreno concluded that, among the shallow plots only, grazing pressure on kelp was likely greatest at ______.

Mean Purple Urchin Density (urchins per square meter)
Site | 5 m depth | 15 m depth
North Cove | 12 | 31
Gull Point | 27 | 9
Ram Reef | 24 | 23
Kelp Hollow | 6 | 14
explanation: The phrase "among the shallow plots only" tells you to use the 5 m column. In that column Gull Point has the highest density, 27 urchins per square meter. More urchins means more grazing, so the statement is only true if it names Gull Point.

A.why: You read the 15 m column. North Cove has the highest density there (31), but the claim is about the shallow plots, and at 5 m North Cove has only 12.

C.why: You probably added the two depths together. Ram Reef has the highest total (47), but the claim covers the shallow plots only, and at 5 m Ram Reef's 24 is below Gull Point's 27.

D.why: You took the right column but went the wrong way. Kelp Hollow has the lowest shallow density (6), so it would have the least grazing pressure, not the most.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Some regional languages keep a "dual" pronoun, a form that refers to exactly two people. Linguist Ana Ferreira recorded everyday conversation in inland and coastal villages where one such language is spoken. Coastal villages have more contact with the national language, which has no dual forms. Ferreira hypothesizes that this contact speeds up the loss of the dual. As evidence, she notes that among speakers aged 30–59 in coastal villages, dual forms appeared in only ______ of utterances.

Use of Dual Pronoun Forms (% of recorded utterances)
Age group | Inland villages | Coastal villages
Under 30 | 14 | 6
30–59 | 41 | 23
60 and older | 68 | 52
explanation: The statement names two things: speakers aged 30–59 and coastal villages. Find the 30–59 row and the Coastal villages column. The cell where they cross is 23%, so that is the only value that makes the statement true.

A.why: You found the right row but read the next column over. 41% is for inland speakers aged 30–59, not coastal ones.

B.why: You found the right column but read the row above. 6% is for coastal speakers under 30, not those aged 30–59.

D.why: You stayed in the coastal column but took the oldest age group. 52% is for coastal speakers 60 and older, and the statement asks about the 30–59 group.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: Fossil leaves can be used to estimate ancient climates. In living forests, trees with toothed leaf edges are more common where temperatures are cool. A smaller share of toothed leaves in a fossil collection therefore points to a warmer climate. A research team studied leaf fossils of the same age from five sites, and Marl Creek produced far more specimens than any other site. The team concluded that the warmest climate among the five sites was at ______.

figure.caption: Share of Fossil Leaves with Toothed Edges, by Site
figure.alt: Bar graph of the percentage of fossil leaves with toothed edges at five sites: Elk Draw 60, Pine Ridge 20, Sawtooth Bench 30, Marl Creek 50, Fern Hollow 70.

explanation: Work out the direction first. Fewer toothed leaves means a warmer climate, so the warmest site has the shortest bar. That is Pine Ridge, at 20%, so only Pine Ridge makes the conclusion true.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. Fern Hollow has the tallest bar (70%), and a large share of toothed leaves points to the coolest climate, not the warmest.

B.why: You knew to look for a short bar but read the one next to it. Sawtooth Bench, at 30%, is the second shortest. Pine Ridge's 20% is lower.

C.why: You picked up a detail from the passage. Marl Creek produced the most specimens, but the number of specimens says nothing about climate, and its 50% toothed share is far from the lowest.

stem: According to the table, which cover treatment did NOT produce a dry-season sorghum yield above 150 bushels per acre?
stimulus:
Agronomists in eastern Nebraska grew sorghum after four different winter cover treatments, then recorded yields in one unusually wet season and one unusually dry one. A cover crop's roots and residue can help soil hold water, so any benefit was expected to show most clearly when rain was scarce. Lead researcher Ana Okafor concluded that, in the dry season, every cover crop yielded more than bare soil did.

Sorghum Yield (bushels per acre)
Cover treatment | Wet season | Dry season
Bare soil | 168 | 131
Cereal rye | 149 | 156
Crimson clover | 147 | 152
Hairy vetch | 142 | 157
explanation: Find the Bare soil row and follow it to the Dry season column: 131 bushels per acre. That is the only dry-season value below 150. The other three are 156, 152 and 157, all above 150.

B.why: You read the Wet season column, where cereal rye has 149. The question asks about the dry season, and there cereal rye has 156, which is above 150.

C.why: You took crimson clover's wet-season value of 147 from the column next door. Its dry-season yield is 152, which is above 150.

D.why: Hairy vetch has the lowest number in the Wet season column (142), so it stood out. But the question names the dry season, and there hairy vetch has 157, the highest value in the column.

stem: According to the graph, which of the following pairings of a meteor shower with its peak hourly count is NOT accurate?
stimulus: Volunteers at a dark-sky reserve in northern Arizona counted meteors during the peak night of five annual showers. They used the same viewing field and the same one-hour window each time, so the counts could be compared fairly. After reviewing the tallies, astronomer Lucía Ferrante claimed that, at this site, only the December shower went above 100 meteors in an hour.

figure.caption: Meteors Counted in the Peak Hour of Five Showers
figure.alt: Bar graph of meteors counted in the peak hour of five showers: Quadrantids, Lyrids, Perseids, Orionids and Geminids, on a vertical scale from 0 to 120 marked every 10.

explanation: The Perseids bar reaches 80, not 30. The value 30 belongs to the Orionids, the bar just to its right. The other three pairings match their bars exactly.

A.why: The Quadrantids bar does reach 50. If you rejected this pairing, your eye probably moved to a neighbouring bar while you followed the gridline across.

B.why: The Lyrids bar reaches 20, so this pairing is accurate. If you rejected it, you may have checked it against the Orionids (30), the other short bar.

D.why: The Geminids bar reaches 110, so this pairing is accurate. You may have rejected it because 110 seemed too high, or because Ferrante's claim made you suspect it. Her claim isn't part of what you're asked. The graph alone decides.

stem: According to the table, which beam's deflection under the 40-tonne load was NOT less than 12 millimeters?
stimulus:
To compare reinforcement materials for a pedestrian bridge, engineers cast four concrete beams with the same span, depth and concrete mix. The only difference was the material used to reinforce each one. They loaded each beam in two stages and measured how far its midpoint sagged. The project lead hypothesized that, at the heavier design load, only the glass-fiber beam would sag past the 12-millimeter limit.

Midspan Deflection (millimeters)
Reinforcement | 40-tonne load | 60-tonne load
Steel rebar | 10 | 15
Carbon fiber | 8 | 12
Basalt fiber | 11 | 16
Glass fiber | 14 | 21
explanation: In the 40-tonne column, glass fiber shows 14 millimeters, which is not less than 12. Steel rebar (10), carbon fiber (8) and basalt fiber (11) are all below 12 at that load.

A.why: You read the 60-tonne column, where steel rebar sags 15 millimeters. Under the 40-tonne load the question names, steel rebar sags 10, which is below 12.

B.why: Carbon fiber's 12 is in the 60-tonne column. Under the 40-tonne load it sags only 8 millimeters, the smallest value in that column.

C.why: Basalt fiber's 11 is close to the limit, and it sits directly above the glass-fiber row. If you slipped down a row you would have read 14. Basalt's own 40-tonne value is 11, which is below 12.
